blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—Motorists can expect slower traffic in parts of Makati City’s central business district from Nov. 14 to Nov. 18. This situation will prevail as police checkpoints, stop-and-go schemes and road rerouting will be implemented during the Asean Summit. The Makati City government announced that portions of major roads will be designated for Asean delegates, with stop-and-go traffic measures in place to allow their convoys to pass. READ: MMDA announces Nov. 15-18 road closures, rerouting for Asean Summit Under the system, motorists may be temporarily held to give way to the convoys.
